title: CANARI: A Monitoring Framework for Cluster Analysis and Node Assessment for Resource Integrity
problem: HPC cluster administrators must balance maintaining up-to-date software versions with system stability to avoid performance degradation, while managing large, complex data centers with many failure points. Continuous monitoring of cluster node availability and performance is needed to detect performance regressions.
motivation: Research computing facilities require automated tools to ensure HPC systems and their software ecosystems maintain expected performance levels.
method: CANARI continuously monitors whether cluster nodes are working and runs test programs (synthetic benchmarks) to measure how fast each node performs. It stores the test results in a database and compares each node's current speed against its normal baseline to identify slowdowns. When nodes show degraded performance, the system automatically stops using them and sends alerts and summary reports to administrators through Slack.
key_novelty: CANARI combines continuous performance monitoring, automated detection of node slowdowns, and immediate Slack alerts into a single system that helps cluster administrators fix problems proactively.
contributions: Monitoring framework for continuous HPC cluster node availability and performance assessment
Automated performance regression detection to identify and isolate degraded nodes
Performance data ingestion and persistent database storage for historical tracking
Real-time alerting system via Slack API for cluster administrators

metrics.other: performance regression detection rate, node availability metrics

primary_theme: HPC cluster monitoring and performance regression detection
